## Goal

Repair the observed dashboard update path with one observation-bound presentation: live capacity, signed selected-volume change, explicit baseline and sample interval, real refresh, separate evidence freshness and a bounded latest-alert record. Prove rendering across sequential samples rather than a single static fixture.

## Deliverables

- Observation-bound live dashboard and real refresh
- Signed interval change and bounded latest-alert presentation
- Rendered-update and lifecycle regression evidence

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AC-TASK-617-01` — First reproduce and qualify the reported freeze with a snapshot-isolated hosted SwiftUI view driven by successive synthetic observations. The visible capacity, change, time and status must update without reopening the popover or clicking refresh; test both an open board and reopening. A changing model getter or one static screenshot is not sufficient evidence.
- `AC-TASK-617-02` — Capacity, health and signed delta derive from the same identified volume and observation. Preserve decreases instead of positive-only aggregation; show no baseline/unknown until two comparable observations exist. Volume changes, restart, pause/resume and stale/failed samples have explicit baseline and freshness behavior; do not invent zero change or use a fresh volume timestamp as detailed-file freshness.
- `AC-TASK-617-03` — The refresh action requests actual new bounded sampling through the existing lifecycle single-flight/cancellation boundary, exposes pending/failure/stale state, and publishes the resulting presentation coherently. Repeated refresh cannot overlap scans, bypass pause/sleep/shutdown controls or turn a cached read into a claimed fresh sample.
- `AC-TASK-617-04` — Display the comparison interval and sample time. Retain at most one latest growth-alert record per app session with its triggering observation/volume, signed amount and interval; subsequent small or negative samples update Recent change without rewriting that alert. Alert retention/restart behavior is explicit. Notifications and dashboard use the same amount/units for the same observation, but different sample intervals are not forced to match. Do not add unbounded alert history or a database migration.
- `AC-TASK-617-05` — Regression coverage includes no baseline, +5.6 GB alert followed by +2.1 MB and a decrease, zero change, delayed/incomplete detail, failure/recovery, pause/resume, single-flight refresh, reopen, volume identity and clean shutdown. Test notification delivery with a fake sink and render the UI in an isolated snapshot under TASK-616 budgets; never send real notifications, open the live database or install a candidate.

## Required Evidence

- `EVREQ-TASK-617-01` (regression-evidence) — A reproducible before/after hosted-view regression that checks visible updates across multiple observations and a fake-notification trace bound to matching observation/interval IDs.
- `EVREQ-TASK-617-02` (regression-evidence) — Bounded lifecycle, signed-volume-delta and presentation test reports covering the acceptance matrix, with candidate hashes, cleanup verification and separate capacity/detail freshness assertions.
